functions.note: before 1.18 Entity.random and Level.random are java.util.Random, whose next(bits) is the same 48-bit step (seed * 0x5DEECE66D + 11 masked to 48 bits, top bits returned); LegacyRandomSource#next only adds a threading check that cannot fire in one thread

java.util.Random.nextInt(bound) before 1.18 is the same rejection loop (and the same power-of-two shortcut); the engine only draws next_int(20) (minecart.rs:1581, MinecartTNT.destroy), which is no power of two, so the loop is the whole method on both sides
java.util.Random.nextFloat before 1.18 is next(24) / (float)(1 << 24), and 5.9604645E-8F is exactly 2^-24, so the product is the same float

java.util.Random.nextDouble before 1.18 is ((long)next(26) << 27 + next(27)) * 0x1.0p-53; BitRandomSource's multiplier is the double constant DOUBLE_MULTIPLIER (1.18 BitRandomSource.java:5, a double field initialised from 1.110223E-16F), which is exactly 2^-53, and the product is a double on both sides

before 1.15 AbstractMinecart keeps the exits as the int[][][] EXITS table indexed by the shape's data (1.14.4 AbstractMinecart.java:716), which lists the same ten pairs in the same order as the 1.15 EnumMap of Pair<Vec3i,Vec3i> (1.15 AbstractMinecart.java:52-72); BlockPos#below's relative(DOWN) is below(1), y - 1, as the const below() here
BlockPos#below() changes from below(1) to relative(Direction.DOWN): both give (x, y - 1, z), which is all below() computes

1.12.2 isRail tests the four rail blocks (rail, powered, detector, activator); from 1.13 the RAILS tag, which in vanilla holds exactly those four. The engine reads TAG_RAIL, which NativeWorldSync sets for exactly these blocks in every release

1.16 adds `getBlock() instanceof BaseRailBlock` to the RAILS tag test; every block of the vanilla RAILS tag is a BaseRailBlock, so the conjunction never differs from the tag alone (only a data pack adding a non-rail block to the tag could tell them apart, which the engine's TAG_RAIL does not model on either side)
1.12.2 isRail tests the four rail blocks, 1.13 the RAILS tag holding the same four; rail_at reads TAG_RAIL and then the state's shape property, which NativeWorldSync gives for exactly those blocks

the added `instanceof BaseRailBlock` cannot exclude a block of the vanilla RAILS tag; and rail_at also requires a parseable RailShape `shape` property, so a non-rail block with the tag (data pack) yields None as the 1.16 instanceof test does
